title: BANG's second war patrol, with SEAHORSE and GROWLER
eyebrow: Marianas lifeguard and Luzon Strait · BANG's second war patrol, in a pack with SEAHORSE and GROWLER
lede: BANG's three torpedo attacks of June and July 1944, as typed on her attack sheets, with her pack-mates' attacks on the same nights and the Japanese record where one has been found. Times are converted to GMT, with Tokyo time alongside.

notes.head: Reading the map.
notes.text: Positions are BANG's own dead reckoning and star sights; lines between them are straight, and where she went in between is not recorded. Open circles are ships she sighted, at the target's position. As the clock passes each firing time a red ring pulses at BANG's position; hover a diamond for the attack sheet.

notes.head: Clocks.
notes.text: BANG kept zone K (−10) for Attack 1 and zone I (−9) for Attacks 2 and 3, as her report does; GROWLER kept I on station, but SEAHORSE kept H (−8). Japanese records use Tokyo time (I, −9): the escort division's chart has HI-67's two oilers hit at 1515, seven minutes after BANG's sheet.

notes.head: What is missing.
notes.text: No Japanese record has been found yet for Attacks 1 and 3; those actions show only the American side. Where the Japanese record names only the ships that were hit, the rest of the convoy is described as the boats saw it.

notes.head: Sources.
notes.text: BANG's second war patrol report, NARA microfilm M1752 (74802784); SEAHORSE Patrol 5 (74845019); GROWLER Patrol 9 (74818866). The 1st Surface Escort Division war diary, June 1944, via JACAR (C08030141000, National Institute for Defense Studies). Sarawak Maru's record from combinedfleet.com, a secondary source, flagged where used. Coastline: Natural Earth.

actions.label: 29 June 1944
actions.ships_note: Only the two ships hit are named in the Japanese record. FRUPAC's map gives the convoy as 1 CVS, 5 escorts and 10 AK/AP.
actions.outcome: Oilers Miri Maru and Sarawak Maru were hit, minor damage, and both reached Manila; neither is in the June list of ships sunk by submarine. BANG claimed two ships sunk and one probably sunk. Her sheet 2(b)'s "large hole under bridge" matches Miri Maru, hit under the bridge. The night before, 28 June, GROWLER sank a large tanker and an escort from a different convoy 130 nm to the northeast (her claim), then left for home on fuel.

events.title: Attack 2
events.text: Torpedo attacks No. 2(a) 2(b) 2(c)
events.outcome: Oilers Miri Maru and Sarawak Maru of HI-67 (Moji to Singapore via Manila), both minor damage; both reached Manila. BANG's sheets claimed 2(a) a large engine-aft freighter or tanker sunk (fits Sarawak Maru, hit in the bow), 2(b) a large passenger freighter sunk with a hole under the bridge (fits Miri Maru, hit under the bridge), and 2(c) a freighter probably sunk (no Japanese record of a third ship hit). FRUPAC relayed the claim as 2 AK sunk, 1 AK probably sunk.

events.title: Ordered 450 ft
events.text: saw second MARU in east column firing what looked like 20 m.m. tracers at us ... range 600 yards so ordered 450 feet.

events.title: Sarawak Maru and Miri Maru
events.text: BANG fires all ten tubes at three ships at about 1510; Sarawak Maru is hit in the bow and Miri Maru under the bridge, and both reach Manila

events.title: Passing 200 ft (1)
events.text: The first depth charge close but above us as we passed 200 feet

events.title: Ordered 500 ft (125)
events.text: A sustained depth charge attack totalling 125 charges started six minutes after the attack. Ran at standard speed for ten minutes then evaded on steady course at 2/3 speed at 500 feet. We were under a 16° negative temperature gradient.

actions.label: 4 July 1944
actions.outcome: No Japanese record of this convoy has been found yet. SEAHORSE attacked first, at 2354–2355 H on 3 July (0054–0055 I), about 13 nm east-northeast of BANG's later attack, and claimed two freighters sunk; BANG fired at 0506 I on what was left of it, and SEAHORSE logged depth charges eleven minutes later "(Bang?)". SEAHORSE attacked again at 1238–1239 H and claimed two passenger freighters sunk. This explains FRUPAC's "torp attack 0105/04".
